name: CRGO Electrical Steel & Transformer Core Localisation
scope: India's import-dependent CRGO and amorphous transformer-steel supply chain, the DGTR anti-dumping probe, domestic capacity build-out (JSW JFE, SAIL, Metglas), and the listed steel makers, core processors and transformer makers exposed to it.

summary.one_line: A quiet week on policy: DGTR has still published no preliminary findings, and Metglas Sri City has still not confirmed its start. The processor sell-off went further. Vilas set a new 52-week low of Rs 266 before recovering to about Rs 306, and Jay Bee hit Rs 65 and closed at Rs 69. A new check adds SAIL, whose CRGO/CRNO plan with John Cockerill is aimed at 2027-29.
key_points: India uses about 400-450 kt of CRGO a year but makes only 40-50 kt, so about 90% is imported (S1). Imports of the products under investigation were worth $821.5m in FY26. China supplied 33.6% of CRGO imports, Japan 31.4%, Russia 20.6% and Korea 6.5% (S4).

DGTR opened the case (F. No. 6/17/2026-DGTR) on 22 Jun 2026 on a petition from JSW JFE Electrical Steel Nashik. It covers China, Japan, Korea and Russia, and the period of investigation is Apr 2025-Mar 2026 (S5, S39). Final findings are due within a year, extendable by six months (S26). As of 28 Nov 2026 our searches found no preliminary findings and no duty.

Processor stocks made new lows this week. Vilas Transcore's 52-week low dropped to Rs 266 from the Rs 301 shown a week earlier, though the stock recovered to close at Rs 305.60 on 27 Nov (1-year -23.6% to -25.3%) (S18). Jay Bee's 52-week low fell to Rs 65, and it closed at Rs 69.00 (1-year -48.0%; market cap about Rs 156 cr) (S41).
JSW Steel, where the JV is immaterial, closed at Rs 1,321.20 on 27 Nov, +13.84% over one year (S44). Screener shows it 4.9% below its 52-week high (S48).

New to coverage: SAIL and John Cockerill India announced a planned $698m plant for CRGO and CRNO electrical steel. It targets 1.5 Mt/yr, with operations slated for 2027-29. The plan stems from an MoU, and we found no 2026 progress update (S45).

Nashik timing: John Cockerill India is supplying the high-temperature tunnel furnaces for Nashik's expansion from 50 to 250 ktpa, with completion targeted for Q1 2027 (S46). JSW JFE plans 350 ktpa in total, with Vijayanagar at full output in 2027 and Nashik phased over 2028-30 (S7, S31).

H1 FY27 results (no change this week). Vilas's PAT fell 29.3% to Rs 17.2 cr on 28% higher volume, and it cut FY27 revenue-growth guidance to 30-35% (S33, S34). Jay Bee's PAT rose 52% to Rs 5.62 cr, but its operating cash flow was -Rs 42.2 cr (S35).
The grid pull is large. The National Electricity Plan budgets Rs 9.15 lakh crore for transmission to 2032 and targets transformation capacity of 2,342 GVA, up from 1,251 GVA (S32).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: JSW Steel, through the 50:50 JSW JFE JV. The JV is the petitioner and the only producer DGTR accepts as domestic industry (S5, S39). A duty would support pricing as Vijayanagar ramps up in 2027 and Nashik in 2028-30 (S31, S46).

Processors that source domestically, or that support the petition. ICRA notes Vilas has diversified to domestic CRGO suppliers (S12). Mangal Electrical, a 16,200 MT processor, registered with DGTR as a supporter of the domestic industry (S5, S22).

Future domestic suppliers inside any duty wall: SAIL's planned CRGO/CRNO plant for 2027-29 (S45), and Proterial's Metglas amorphous plant at Sri City (about 30 kt/yr; 74:26 with unlisted Shirdi Sai), which targeted an Oct 2026 start that we have not seen confirmed (S16).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Transformer makers that import CRGO. Indo Tech registered with DGTR as user and importer, and TARIL as importer (S5). TARIL says CRGO is 33-35% of its raw-material cost (S10). TERI estimates that a 10% CRGO price rise adds 1.5-3% to transformer cost (S11).

Processors with stretched working capital. Vilas's inventory rose to Rs 115.4 cr from Rs 72.3 cr in six months (S33). Jay Bee burned Rs 42.2 cr of operating cash in H1 and its short-term debt nearly tripled (S35). Jay Bee's market cap is now about Rs 156 cr (S41).
For JSW Steel the payoff is small and late. The JV is unlisted and 50%-owned (S7). JSW has trailing sales of Rs 1.99 lakh crore (S48), and most new capacity arrives in 2027-30 (S31).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: DGTR preliminary findings, if any, or the final findings due by about 22 Jun 2027 (extendable to about Dec 2027), followed by any government notification (S5, S26).
Completion of the Nashik tunnel furnaces, targeted for Q1 2027 (S46), and Vijayanagar's full production in 2027 (S31).

Whether Vilas defends its Rs 266 low and delivers 26,000+ MT of CRGO volume in FY27 (S18, S34); whether Jay Bee's operating cash flow turns positive in H2 (S35); and confirmation that Metglas Sri City has started (S16).

subsections.title: What CRGO and amorphous metal are

blocks.text: Cold-rolled grain-oriented (CRGO) electrical steel and amorphous metal are the core materials of power and distribution transformers. About 98% of CRGO output goes into transformers (S11). Amorphous ribbon, such as Proterial's Metglas, cuts transformer no-load losses and can reduce standby power use by about one-third compared with conventional electrical sheet (S16). The DGTR case covers both materials (S5).

The supply chain has three layers. Steel mills make the CRGO coil. Processors slit, cut and assemble it into laminations and cores: Vilas, Jay Bee, Mangal, and TARIL's POSCO Poggenamp unit. Transformer makers come last (S10, S12, S22). Estimates of CRGO's cost share differ because they use different bases. TARIL puts it at 33-35% of raw-material cost (S10). TERI puts it at 15-20% of a standard transformer's bill of materials, while an MSME source quoted 40-50% (S11).

blocks.text: BIS licensing already acts as a non-tariff gate, because imported CRGO must be BIS-certified. GTRI argues that this makes the dispute about price, not quality, and that with domestic output under one-tenth of demand, a duty mainly raises costs rather than displacing imports (S1). Because the probe covers four supplier countries that together provide over 90% of CRGO imports (S4), a duty would leave little cheap supply that does not pay it.

blocks.text: GTRI's case against a duty: CRGO was previously left out of safeguard duties because India depends on imports, and with domestic output under one-tenth of demand a duty mainly raises transformer and grid costs (S1). The Indian Steel Association replies that CRGO needs 7-10 times the investment per tonne of conventional steel, and that subsidised imports threaten that investment (S11). An MSME federation official says JSW is 'the only beneficiary' (S11).

Opposition is broad. DGTR's interested-party list includes the Embassy of Japan, Russia's Ministry of Economic Development, IEEMA, KOSA and the China Iron and Steel Association, plus several listed transformer makers (S5). Indian rules set no fixed deadline for preliminary findings (S26), so the timing of any interim duty is uncertain. Five months after initiation, we still found none.

blocks.text: The National Electricity Plan (Transmission) budgets Rs 9.15 lakh crore to 2032. It takes the transmission network from 4.85 lakh ckm to 6.48 lakh ckm, and transformation capacity at 220 kV and above from 1,251 GVA to 2,342 GVA (S32). KNN gives a 1,290 GVA base for the same target (S11). On our arithmetic, even the full 350 ktpa from the JV plus 30 kt of amorphous ribbon is below today's 400-450 kt demand (S1, S16, S31). SAIL's 1.5 Mt/yr plan could close the gap, but its CRGO share, its site and its final approval are all unconfirmed (S45). Imports should therefore remain the marginal supply through at least 2028.

blocks.text: Falling CRGO prices, not the probe, still drive processor P&Ls. Vilas grew volume 28% but revenue only 6%, and its gross margin fell 255 bps (S33). Jay Bee's manufacturing revenue fell about 17% (our arithmetic) as material cost dropped to Rs 146.2 cr from Rs 181.2 cr, and its profit came from better margins and EPC work (S35). A duty would reverse the price trend. Processors that pass costs through would book inventory gains, and any lag would compress margins that ICRA already flags as sensitive to CRGO prices, with no formal hedging (S12). Vilas is diversifying into nanocrystalline cores, radiators and copper conductors (S33).

JSW Steel holds 50% of the JV and JFE holds the rest (S7). Screener shows JSW's trailing consolidated sales at Rs 1,99,021 cr and PAT at Rs 31,708 cr (S48). As an illustration only (our arithmetic, not a forecast): 350 ktpa at the Rs 190-195/kg CRGO price Vilas cited in Aug 2026 (S13) gives about Rs 6,650-6,825 cr of gross revenue for the whole JV. That is about 3.4% of JSW's trailing sales, roughly 1.7% for JSW's 50% share, and it would build only over 2027-30 (S31).

SAIL, a state-owned steel maker, has announced a roughly $698m CRGO/CRNO plant with John Cockerill India, to be fed with SAIL hot-rolled coil and slated for 2027-29 (S45). It qualifies as an electrical-steel maker on announced intent only. We found no investment approval, site or 2026 progress, and SAIL is not a party to the DGTR case as domestic industry (S5, S45).

Downstream, DGTR registrants include CG Power (user industry and exporter/producer), Hitachi Energy India, Indo Tech (user and importer), TARIL (importer), Atlanta Electricals and BHEL (S5). TARIL has partly hedged by buying 51% of POSCO Poggenamp, a 24,000 t/yr CRGO processor (S10). TERI estimates that a 10% CRGO price rise adds 1.5-3% to transformer cost, and a 20% rise adds 3-6% (S11).

items: GTRI (Ajay Srivastava): a duty raises transformer and grid costs but gives little protection, because domestic output is under one-tenth of demand (S1, S4).
TERI (Alekhya Datta): a 10% CRGO price rise adds 1.5-3% to transformer cost, and a 20% rise adds 3-6% (S11).
Indian Steel Association (Alok Sahay): domestic CRGO capacity is capital-intensive, and subsidised imports threaten investment (S11).
ICRA (Vilas, Jul 2025): [ICRA]A- (Stable)/A2+, balancing strong interest cover against working-capital intensity, customer concentration and exposure to CRGO prices (S12).
Vilas management (Nov 2026 call): about 10% EBITDA margin now and 11-12% at peak; a long-term target of Rs 1,000 cr revenue at peak utilisation (S34).

blocks.text: Coverage is still thin. This week we again found no sell-side initiation or sector note framing JSW Steel, SAIL, Vilas, Jay Bee or Mangal as a CRGO localisation play. Discussion is limited to retail results aggregators and price pages (S18, S33, S34, S35, S41).

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.caption: Stock performance (latest dated readings found; the dashboard shows today's numbers)

blocks.text: What changed since the 21 Nov edition: Vilas broke below its earlier Rs 301 low to a new 52-week low of Rs 266, then recovered to Rs 305.60 by 27 Nov. Its 1-month return is still -15.23% (S18). Jay Bee made a new low of Rs 65 and closed at Rs 69.00, about 4% below last week's Rs 72 reading (S41). JSW Steel edged down to Rs 1,321.20 but is still up about 14% over one year (S44). With no news on the probe, the processors' moves reflect thin margins and cash-flow strain, not the CRGO theme.

items: The duty could be rejected or diluted. Opposition is organised, including foreign governments, industry associations and large user-industry registrants (S5), and GTRI and TERI stress the cost to the grid (S1, S11).
Timing mismatch: final findings may not come until Jun-Dec 2027 (S26), while Nashik's expansion phases in only over 2028-30 (S31, S46).
Price volatility squeezing processors. Vilas's H1 EBITDA fell 20% on 28% higher volume (S33), and Mangal's Q2 operating profit fell 29.4% (S30).

Working capital and liquidity. Jay Bee's H1 operating cash flow was -Rs 42.2 cr and its short-term debt rose to Rs 74.3 cr (S35). The market caps are tiny: Jay Bee about Rs 156 cr, Vilas about Rs 748 cr (S41, S18).
Guidance risk. Vilas has already cut its FY27 growth guidance from 45-50% to 30-35% (S13, S34).
Materiality for the large caps. JSW's JV is unlisted, 50%-owned and small next to group sales (S7, S48). SAIL's plan is still only an announcement (S45).

companies.name: JSW Steel
companies.role: Owns 50% of JSW JFE Electrical Steel. The JV's Nashik CRGO plant (50 ktpa) is the DGTR petitioner, and the JV is expanding to 350 ktpa across Nashik and Vijayanagar (S5, S7, S31).
companies.impact: The JV is the main beneficiary of any duty (S11). At full capacity it is roughly 3% of JSW's trailing sales before applying JSW's 50% share (our arithmetic; S13, S48), and the capacity arrives over 2027-30 (S31, S46). The stock is +13.84% over one year (S44).

companies.role: State-owned steel maker planning a roughly $698m, 1.5 Mt/yr CRGO and CRNO electrical-steel plant with John Cockerill India, fed with SAIL hot-rolled coil (S45).
companies.impact: A potential future domestic CRGO supplier inside any duty wall, but only at the announcement stage: operations are slated for 2027-29, with no approval, site or 2026 update found (S45). It is not the DGTR petitioner (S5).

companies.impact: H1 FY27 PAT rose 52% to Rs 5.62 cr, but operating cash flow was -Rs 42.2 cr and short-term debt nearly tripled (S35). The stock is -47.97% over one year, at Rs 69.00 with a market cap of about Rs 156 cr (S41).

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W47 edition (21 Nov 2026), researched on 28 Nov 2026 with web search and direct page fetches. We re-searched for DGTR preliminary findings or a duty notification, a Metglas Sri City start and new JSW JFE announcements and found none dated after the last edition, so those items carry forward as unchanged. New this week: refreshed 27 Nov prices for Vilas (Anand Rathi, S18; the page again shows two inconsistent sets of 6-month and 1-year returns, so both are given, and IndMoney independently showed the same Rs 266 52-week low), Jay Bee (Upstox, S41, consistent with Screener's Rs 69.2 and Rs 156 cr) and JSW Steel (Upstox, S44, plus Screener, S48, for trailing sales, PAT and distance from the 52-week high). We added SAIL after a broader search across steel majors turned up its CRGO/CRNO plan with John Cockerill (S45); we found no 2026 progress and treat it as an announcement only. We found no CRGO plans from Tata Steel or JSPL. We also added John Cockerill's Nashik tunnel-furnace contract (S46) as the dated 'furnace delivery' catalyst. JSW's earnings base now uses Screener trailing figures (S48) instead of the Q2 news article. Dropped as stale or no longer needed: the 11 Nov JSW price (S36), the 20 Nov Jay Bee price (S37), the 20 Nov Mangal price page (S38, since neither it nor numbers.json gave a fresh price), the 2024 BIS shortage article (S27) and the JSW Q2 article (S21). A search-result summary claimed Vilas's H1 FY27 PAT 'improved 13.5%'. That contradicts the -29.3% in S33 and was not confirmed, so it is not used. A Screener note of a 20 Nov CARE rating update for Jay Bee could not be opened, so it is not used. Carried-forward figures (GTRI balance, import mix, JV capex, ICRA, TARIL, TERI, H1 results, the DGTR interested-party list) come from previously fetched sources. Producer coverage is JSW Steel plus SAIL's announced plan. NLMK India and Shirdi Sai Electricals appear unlisted, and Voltamp and Shilchar were again left out for lack of a citable CRGO link. Revenue arithmetic is our own and labelled as such. No ratings or price targets. Source IDs are not contiguous.
